title: Wine Wimsey Review · Sat Nov 28
subtitle: Batch date Sat Nov 28 (EVEN day): characters at feed slots 1,3,5,7; plain cards at 2,4,6. 7 feed posts + 2 stories, no captions or first comments. Characters: Hot Mess (#1 + story 1), Homebody (#3), Bold One (#5), Settled One (#7 + story 2). Seasonal: 3 of 7 feed (plain #2, characters #3 and #5) + 1 story (Christmas shopping). Quotes: 2 spun (#4 phone-down-a-rabbit-hole, #6 hit-and-run, both new jokes), 0 inbox (inbox empty), 7 original. Weekday references: none. Credits: 6 first pass + 3 regenerations (#1 had a car in frame with wine, #3 and #7 had pets) = 9 x 45 = 405 credits; plain cards free. Image checks: every quote matches word for word, no animals, no cars, no stray logos, all drawn cartoons. Note: recent batches (Nov 23-27) were the NEW-VOICE format (8 posts with captions); this run followed the stored nightly prompt (7+2 plain/character, no captions). Tell me if the nightly task should switch.

stories.quote: EVERY YEAR I PROMISE TO FINISH MY CHRISTMAS SHOPPING EARLY. EVERY YEAR I'M IN A PARKING LOT ON THE 23RD, FIGHTING A STRANGER FOR THE LAST GIFT SET.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy bun with a pencil in it and grey-streaked hair in a winter coat, tugging a boxed gift set back and forth with a scowling cartoon stranger in a knit cap in a store parking lot at dusk, holding a glass of red wine. Text in a speech bubble at the top reads: Every year I promise to finish my Christmas shopping early. Every year I'm in a parking lot on the 23rd, fighting a stranger for the last gift set.

stories.quote: MY LAUNDRY BASKET AND I HAVE AN AGREEMENT. I FILL IT, IT HOLDS, AND NEITHER OF US MENTIONS THE CLEAN CLOTHES ON THE CHAIR.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a barefoot woman with silver-white hair and lavender glasses in a sage cardigan, standing calmly in a bedroom beside an overflowing laundry basket and a chair stacked with folded clothes, holding a glass of red wine. Text in a speech bubble at the top reads: My laundry basket and I have an agreement. I fill it, it holds, and neither of us mentions the clean clothes on the chair.

posts.quote: I TURNED MY HEAD TO CHECK FOR TRAFFIC AND HEARD A NOISE LIKE A BAG OF WALNUTS. THE TRAFFIC WAS FINE. MY NECK WASN'T.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy bun with a pencil in it, grey-streaked auburn hair, an olive vest and a striped shirt, standing on a city sidewalk with a wince, one hand on the back of her neck and a paper coffee cup in the other. Text in a speech bubble at the top reads: I turned my head to check for traffic and heard a noise like a bag of walnuts. The traffic was fine. My neck wasn't.

posts.quote: The stuffing tastes better on day three. It's the only thing in this family that improves with time.
posts.alt: Plain off-white quote card with centered bold dark text. Text reads: The stuffing tastes better on day three. It's the only thing in this family that improves with time.

posts.quote: I'VE BEEN IN THE SAME SWEATPANTS SINCE THE PIE AND I'M NOT SORRY. THE COUCH AND I HAVE A STANDING ARRANGEMENT NOW.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a laughing woman with short mauve-pink curls in a mustard knit sweater, grey sweatpants and pink slippers, reclined in a floral armchair under a pink blanket with a glass of red wine, a slice of pie on the side table beside a fireplace. Text in a speech bubble at the top reads: I've been in the same sweatpants since the pie and I'm not sorry. The couch and I have a standing arrangement now.

posts.quote: I picked up my phone to check what time the post office closes. Forty minutes later I was pricing a train across Canada and watching a man restore a rusty wheelbarrow. The post office closed at five.
posts.alt: Plain off-white quote card with centered bold dark text. Text reads: I picked up my phone to check what time the post office closes. Forty minutes later I was pricing a train across Canada and watching a man restore a rusty wheelbarrow. The post office closed at five.

posts.quote: MY NEIGHBOR HAS HIS CHRISTMAS LIGHTS UP AND IT'S STILL NOVEMBER. I HAVEN'T EVEN FINISHED THE PIE. I ADMIRE THE CONFIDENCE AND I RESENT THE LADDER.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a huge halo of copper curls, round glasses and gold hoop earrings in a patterned tunic and coat, one palm raised and a glass of red wine in the other hand, giving a side-eye toward a neighbor's house covered in Christmas lights with a ladder against it. Text in a speech bubble at the top reads: My neighbor has his Christmas lights up and it's still November. I haven't even finished the pie. I admire the confidence and I resent the ladder.

posts.quote: Everyone says life flies by. Mine sideswipes me in a parking lot and drives off without leaving a note.
posts.alt: Plain off-white quote card with centered bold dark text. Text reads: Everyone says life flies by. Mine sideswipes me in a parking lot and drives off without leaving a note.

posts.quote: SOMEONE ASKED WHERE I SEE MYSELF IN TEN YEARS. IN THIS SAME CHAIR, WITH A SLIGHTLY BETTER CUSHION.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a barefoot woman with silver-white wavy hair and round lavender glasses in an oatmeal sweater and sage joggers, relaxed in a brown armchair in a sunny room full of plants, holding a mug with a glass of red wine on the side table. Text in a speech bubble at the top reads: Someone asked where I see myself in ten years. In this same chair, with a slightly better cushion.
